lessonTitle: 4. The definite integral; the Newton-Leibniz formula
lessonTitleEnglish: The definite integral; the Newton-Leibniz formula
source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 12 mathematics textbooks (advanced stream)

stages.headline: The area of the curvilinear trapezoid under y = f(x) ≥ 0 between x = a, x = b and the x-axis is the integral of f from a to b.
stages.headlineEnglish: The area of the curvilinear trapezoid under y = f(x) ≥ 0 between x = a, x = b and the x-axis is the integral of f from a to b.

stages.headline: The Newton-Leibniz formula: the integral from a to b equals F(b) − F(a), where F is any antiderivative of f.
stages.headlineEnglish: The Newton-Leibniz formula: the integral from a to b equals F(b) − F(a), where F is any antiderivative of f.

stages.headline: Example: the integral of sin x from 0 to π is −cos π + cos 0 = 2; integrals split over sums and constant factors.
stages.headlineEnglish: Example: the integral of sin x from 0 to π is −cos π + cos 0 = 2; integrals split over sums and constant factors.
